reading.text:
Common setting (paper §1-§2, used by every reading below). Horizon T>0, dimensions n,m,d>=1.
H = R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x L^2(nu;R^m) with the l^2-combined norm
|theta|_H^2 = |x|^2+|y|^2+|z|_F^2+||u||_{L^2(nu)}^2 (Euclidean on vectors, Frobenius on matrices,
L^2(nu) on the fibre; u an a.e.-class). P_2(H): Borel probability measures on H with finite second
moment, metrised by W_2 built on |.|_H. Coefficients are deterministic functions
b:[0,T]xHxP_2(H)->R^n, sigma:->R^{n x d}, h:->L^2(nu;R^n), f:->R^m, g:R^n x P_2(R^n)->R^m.
Diagonal input at t: Theta in L^2(Omega,F_t;H) on the standing basis together with mu=Law(Theta).
All hypotheses are diagonal (mu never varied independently of Theta), interior ones for a.e. t in
[0,T] with the null time set chosen before the inputs, terminal ones for all X_T,X'_T in
L^2(Omega,F_T;R^n) with induced laws rho=Law(X_T). The standing filtration is the usual augmentation
of the one generated by W, N and an independent F_0. Since the stability constant is claimed
dimension-free, norm choices matter: Euclidean/Frobenius/L^2(nu) norms (or a choice differing from
them only by dimension-free factors) are required wherever a definition enters a quantitative bound.

UNIT def:Dissertation.WellPosedness.System.Coeffs.mk
Paper notion: the constructor of the coefficient system (b,sigma,h,f,g) (see the reading of
System.Coeffs): given the five deterministic functions with the signatures of §2, form the system.
Faithful iff its arguments are exactly the five fields of a faithful Coeffs (no extra data, no
proof obligations beyond what Coeffs requires).

comparison.text:
Comparison: constructor System.Coeffs.mk vs locked reading.
Its five arguments are exactly the fields b, σ, h, f, g of Coeffs with their types (time ℝ,
TupleH, P2 TupleH; σ into EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n × Fin d); h into Lp (ℝⁿ) 2 ν; g on ℝⁿ × P2 ℝⁿ),
returning Coeffs ν n m d; no extra data or proof obligations. Meaning that of Coeffs.
Verdict: faithful with representation choices (those of Coeffs).

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. Time ranges over ℝ rather than [0,T]; only [0,T] (or (0,T)) enters every predicate on the
   coefficients, so the values off the horizon are unused.
2. ℝ^{n×d} (σ) and ℝ^{m×d} (the Z-slot) are EuclideanSpace ℝ on the index pairs (i,j), whose
   norm and inner product are the Frobenius ones.
3. The tuple space H is the product with the maximum of the four channel norms; it has the same
   topology, Borel sets and P₂ as the Hilbert-norm H, and the assumptions use the channel norms
   and the Hilbert-norm W₂ (w2H) explicitly.
4. The measure argument is the structure P2 (a probability measure with finite second moment),
   i.e. P₂(H) and P₂(ℝⁿ) as sets of laws; the fibre and h's values are Lp classes.
